name: Deep Western Boundary Current
scope: North Atlantic study-section reach from 47 degrees N to 24.5 degrees N via a coarse western-boundary reference corridor. Excludes upstream subpolar circulation, interior pathways, recirculation and tropical/South Atlantic continuation. Not the whole DWBC or a continuous observed deep-water pathway.
layer: Source-defined deep circulation: around 2800 m to bottom at 47 degrees N, around 2682 m to bottom at 36 degrees N, and around 2500–5500 m at 24.5 degrees N. Interfaces vary by section; no common fixed-depth axis reconstructed.
time_convention: Editorial route linking source section latitudes; not a simultaneous measured trajectory or a 1990–2019 mean current axis.
source_locator: Section 3.2.3 and Figure 8/Table 3: DWBC sections at 47, 36 and 24.5 degrees N, section-specific deep interfaces and western Atlantic boundary geography. Section widths are not along-current lengths.
source_citation: Caínzos et al. (2023), Consistent picture of the horizontal circulation of the Atlantic Ocean over 3 decades, Ocean Science 19, 1009–1045.
source_license: Factual geographic references only; no source prose, figures, provider geometry or model data packaged.
coordinate_selection: OSW selects coarse offshore waypoints from the Grand Banks region toward the Bahamas. Source section locations constrain latitude and deep-flow identity; these intermediate coordinates are not published axes or diagnosed bathymetric contours. Continuity between sections remains an assumption.
scenario_rule: Three uniform longitude offsets (-0.5/0/+0.5 degrees) crossed with three independent endpoint latitude offsets (-0.5/0/+0.5 degrees): 27 editorial scenarios. This limited corridor sensitivity does not encompass interior pathways or establish a continuous observed current.
remaining_gates: Independent scientific review of the chosen boundary corridor, section joins and interior pathway alternatives.
Validate deep route with bathymetry and layer-specific velocity geometry; coarse surface-land clearance is insufficient.
Keep study reach excluded from whole-current ordering; canonical integration and publication review required.
